method.captures: Four matched views per tab using seed 0x51a7e3 and controlled browser clocks. Auto and Welcome use the original presets. Lighter and Darker change the host CSS background from the Welcome preset. Embedded and opaque canvases retain their own drawing rules.
method.contrast: Named pixel from the Welcome capture compared directly with each specified swatch using sRGB relative luminance. pixels stores the actual captured pixel at that coordinate for each variant.
method.motion: 36 adjacent canvas pairs 2/60 s apart. Nearest-neighbor grid 160 columns, height limited to 32–128. A pixel changes if the largest absolute RGBA channel difference reaches 16/255. Fractions refer to the grid on the selected canvas.
method.cadence: Separate native-clock headless foreground Chrome run, 15 warm-up intervals then 90 intervals per tab, including active Stretch. Median and nearest-rank 95th percentile. Blank-page baselines before and after.
method.limits: One desktop viewport and one recorded scenario per tab plus the named targeted probes. Source observations cover some other controls. Timing depends on hardware, browser and load.

tab.name: Sand
tab.feature: Gold sand in the welcome pile
tab.note: A stored phase offsets each loose grain. It keeps the same position while settled. Sparkles have a separate fade, and stamped letters have a Shimmer switch.

tab.name: Loop
tab.note: Orbit radii breathe with elapsed time. Angular motion advances once per frame. The trail reuses the previous image, so repainting can change its brightness even at a fixed position.

tab.name: Bubbles
tab.note: A bubble receives its hue and initial velocity when it forms. Dragging, release, wall bounces and merging can change its speed or position abruptly.

tab.name: Plate
tab.feature: Gold grains on a node line
tab.note: The shared grain solver adds random kicks to velocity. Freeze skips grain integration. A grain can visibly shake while finding a node.

tab.name: Crystal
tab.note: Newly frozen facets receive random lighting, then their pixels are cached. Rebuilding that layer draws fresh lighting on existing cells. The glint animation has its own clock.

tab.name: Magnets
tab.feature: Cyan rim of the magnetic fluid
tab.note: The field moves the fluid particles. Adding fluid copies and offsets existing particle positions. Pausing and dragging a magnet exercise different paths.

tab.name: Stretch
tab.note: While running, the solver repeatedly advances within one drawing callback with a 28 ms work budget. The color comparison uses its paused initial field. The frame-timing run uses the active solver.
tab.action: initial field paused for the matched shots; active solver timed separately

tab.name: Ferro
tab.feature: Body of the central ferrofluid drop
tab.note: Tracer positions are resampled when their lifetime ends. The physics uses elapsed time with a 5 to 33 ms clamp. The Welcome Navy setting already selects the lighter shade for Ferro.

tab.note: The default chart is drawn on input. Playback advances the slider after at least 65 ms, so its steps are visible even when the browser is delivering frames evenly.

tab.name: Ring
tab.note: The breathing ring adds 0.035 radians on every animation callback. The same elapsed second advances the phase twice as far at 120 callbacks as at 60.

tab.name: Zeros
tab.feature: Amber marker on the gap map
tab.note: The opening gap map redraws on parameter or point changes. The separate spacing demo generates a random comparison set, and the tightrope has its own timed drawing loop.

tab.name: Pendulum
tab.note: A small fast-moving spot triggered the existing Play guard. After Play, the pendulum uses elapsed time capped at 50 ms. The guarded and playing canvases were sampled separately.
tab.action: after pressing the existing Play control

tab.name: Trilogy
tab.feature: Blue node on the line graph
tab.note: The default line evolves with the selected equation. In the Cube view the optional camera rotation adds a fixed angle per frame. Selecting random data redraws the starting state.

tab.name: Black Hole
tab.feature: Blue point on a light ray
tab.note: Stars are generated once. Each displayed simulation frame advances the light rays by eight solver steps. Render timing affects playback speed while the capture rule still uses the simulated path.

tab.name: Ocean
tab.note: Globe rotation and wave phase use elapsed time capped at 50 ms. The ocean solver divides that interval into four steps. The plotted time series is sampled separately.

tab.name: 4D
tab.feature: Violet point on the projected surface
tab.note: Drift integrates elapsed time with a 50 ms cap. Camera movement and the projected surface can move thin edges across pixels as the geometry rotates.

tab.name: Polychora
tab.note: Rotation uses elapsed time capped at 50 ms. Projected wire edges can jump from one screen pixel to the next without a fresh random vertex.

tab.name: Fireflies
tab.note: The opening cymatics view pulses after Play. A separate Fireflies mode adds random velocity kicks and couples phase between insects. The startup guard covers both views.
tab.action: after pressing the existing Play control

tab.name: Horned
tab.feature: Pink branch of the horned sphere
tab.note: With rotation enabled, the camera adds 0.004 radians per animation frame. A higher refresh rate changes the rate at which fine branches sweep across the screen.

tab.name: Non-Orientable
tab.note: The surface animation increments its clock by 0.016 per draw. Thin mesh lines and the moving traveler can cross pixels even along a smooth path.

tab.name: 5D / E₈
tab.feature: Gold point of the E8 projection
tab.note: Auto-Drift adds 0.008 to its time variable on every render. Dragging or toggling drift changes how the projected points move.

tab.name: Leech
tab.feature: Pale center of the Leech point cloud
tab.note: The opening Cloud view redraws on input and selection. The original rotating view adds 0.003 per frame when enabled. The two views have different motion behavior.

tab.name: 5D Lite
tab.note: This archived view advances its time by 0.01 per frame while running. Pausing holds that clock. Point motion follows the projection.

tab.name: Hopf
tab.note: The time variable advances by 0.016 per frame. A translucent dark fill fades earlier fibers every draw. Speed and the trail length in seconds can vary with the display rate.

tab.name: Black Hole B
tab.note: This archived lensing view generates the stars once. Its ray loop checks capture before movement and runs three solver steps per displayed frame.

tab.name: Black Hole C (Disk) v2
tab.note: Disk particle positions and sizes are chosen at creation. Ringdown can spawn ripples at random on later frames. The archived tab opens in lensing mode.

tab.name: E₈ → Milnor
tab.note: Auto-orbit adds a fixed 0.004 radians on each drawing frame while the pointer is free. The stepped movement comes from projected geometry.

tab.name: E₈ Inspector
tab.feature: Gold point in the E₈ projection
tab.note: The root projection redraws when a preset, selection, angle or projection changes. Its default view held still throughout the motion sample.

tab.name: E₈ → Milnor v2
tab.note: Auto-orbit adds 0.004 radians per draw, multiplied by one minus the face-on blend. A fully face-on projection removes that automatic rotation.

tab.name: Unit Distances
tab.feature: Orange spoke of the selected grid point
tab.note: Controls redraw the grid, and resizing schedules one update. The default drawing held still throughout the motion sample.

tab.name: Cipher Inspector
tab.note: The heatmap starts idle. Starting the annealer advances a stochastic search. Its roughness readout describes the plotted score history. The optional mandala spin uses a separate loop.

tab.name: More materials
tab.note: A settled cell is drawn from its neighbors. Exposure gives #323A4A and enclosure gives #010101. Randomness in pouring and sliding can move grains. A fixed settled pile kept the same edge.

tab.name: Feathers and Bricks
tab.note: Still air holds the pile. Wind combines three sine waves and sways loose feathers. Text readings refresh about every quarter-second, on a separate schedule from the drawing.
